Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Augmented and Virtual Reality [CSE_4051]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain with a suitable example how the Three I's of Virtual Reality guide the design of a VR-based (5)  
  virtual classroom for interactive learning.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           A company is developing an immersive temple exploration experience using AR/VR technologies.         (5)  
  i) Analyze the key characteristics of VR that enhance virtual heritage experiences.  
  ii) Discuss how AR can complement VR in providing contextual cultural information.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                A global company is designing a VR workspace where users perform static, dynamic, symbolic, and (5)  
  manipulative gestures to interact.  
  A)           Apply suitable techniques for real-time gesture input mapping and synchronization of multiple users  
  within the shared virtual environment.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A smart city AR navigation app guides pedestrians using arrows on the screen, voice directions,      (5)  
  and subtle vibrations when taking turns.  
  i) Analyze how visual and auditory feedback together help users follow the correct route.  
  ii) Analyze how haptic cues improve user safety and attention in busy environments.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                A VR archaeological exploration app allows users to walk through a recreated ancient city using      (5)  
  full-body tracking and multimodal feedback. Apply your understanding of AR/VR interface  
  A)           technologies to improve immersion.  
  i) Explain how 3D position trackers can help users navigate archaeological sites accurately.  
  ii) Apply binaural and ambisonic audio techniques to guide users to hidden artifacts or important  
  locations.  
  iii) Illustrate the use of tactile feedback when users virtually touch artifacts.  
  iv) Discuss how gesture-based manipulation can allow object inspection from different angles.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A VR art museum lets users experience paintings and sculptures through multiple sensory outputs. (5)  
  i) Analyze how geometric modelling enhance the visual realism of paintings and sculptures.  
  ii) Examine how 3D spatial sound contributes to immersion while exploring the museum  
  environment.  
  
  Page #1

iii) Discuss the role of haptic feedback and behavior/kinematic modelling in making sculpture  
  interaction feel authentic.  
  iv) Evaluate challenges in synchronizing visual, audio, haptics feedback without overwhelming the  
  user.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)              A mobile AR device uses incremental tracking while performing SLAM during user movement.            (5)  
  i) Apply the motion model concept to explain how predicting the next feature location helps reduce  
  A)         computation during tracking.  
  ii) Apply the combined detection and tracking approach to explain how the device maintains reliable  
  feature points when some are lost from view. Draw a simple block diagram showing how detection  
  and tracking work together in the process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Distributed VR systems use side-by-side displays and PC clusters to support multi-user immersive (5)  
  environments.  
  i) Analyze how synchronization methods (software, frame-buffer, and video synchronization) impact  
  performance and visual consistency in these architectures.  
  ii) Support your answer with a simplified diagram of synchronized rendering pipelines.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              A robotic arm model in an AR-based manufacturing simulator must position its gripper accurately to (5)  
  pick up tools from a workbench.  
  A)         Apply kinematic modeling by describing:  
  i) The application of kinematic chain elements (links, joints, actuators) in determining the robot's  
  reachable workspace.  
  ii) The application of numerical inverse kinematics in updating joint angles when the target tool  
  moves slightly, while avoiding unnatural or impossible poses.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         In a collaborative VR design platform, multiple users can modify the same 3D model of a car at the    (5)  
  same time. Some users report inconsistencies, changes made on one headset do not instantly  
  appear on others.  
  i) Analyze the need for model synchronization in multi-user VR and its impact on interactivity.  
  ii) Explain how model hierarchy or scene graph can help maintain consistency during real-time  
  updates.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
